resources.name: Alley Pond Environmental Center, Inc
resources.mission: The Alley Pond Environmental Center (APEC), a nonprofit environmental education organization, is dedicated to educating children and adults in the New York metropolitan area, protecting and preserving Alley Pond Park, open spaces and waterbodies, and advocating for sustainable environmental policies and practices.
resources.fees: There is no fee to visit the center but there are fees to attend programs.

resources.name: Commonpoint NY
resources.address: 58-20 Little Neck Parkway, Little Neck, NY 11362
resources.mission: Commonpoint is a social services organization that meets the diverse needs of New York City and beyond. We offer a wide range of programs for people of all ages, ability levels, and backgrounds to connect and grow together.
resources.languages: English, Spanish, Russian, Bukhrarian, Mandarin, Creole, Hebrew, Farsi, Urdu, Hindi, Pashto, French

resources.name: Friends of Crocheron & John Golden Park
resources.mission: The mission of Friends of Crocheron & John Golden Park is to promote the preservation and enjoyment of Crocheron Park and John Golden Park, to sponsor educational, cultural, and community service events for the park, and to raise funds for the restoration and enhancement of the park in the community-oriented spirit of John Golden.

resources.name: Korean American Youth Choir of New York
resources.address: 4001 Little Neck Pkwy #31B, Little Neck, NY 11363
resources.mission: The Korean American Youth Choir of New York (KAYCNY) is dedicated to inspiring young voices, fostering cultural pride, and building bridges across communities through the power of music. We provide youth with high-quality choral training and performance opportunities that celebrate Korean heritage while embracing diversity and inclusion. Our mission is to nurture the next generation of leaders and artists who will share harmony, unity, and cultural understanding both locally and globally.
resources.fees: No, but any donation is welcome.

resources.name: Little Neck-Douglaston Community Ambulance Corps, Inc. (LNDCAC)
resources.address: 42-18 Marathon Parkway, Little Neck, New York 11363
resources.mission: Located in northeast Queens in New York City, LNDCAC is a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization and New York State certified Basic Life Support Emergency Medical Service agency run solely on the selfless time and dedication of non-paid community volunteers. LNDCAC also serves as a proud New York City 911 participating member, assisting the Fire Department of New York City's Bureau of Emergency Medical Services (FDNY EMS) throughout the five boroughs of New York City. (A) To provide ambulance service without charge, to help, aid, and assist persons who are sick, infirm, or otherwise disabled by supplying emergency transportation to, from, or between hospitals and/or nursing homes within a 50- mile radius of Little Neck & Douglaston, County of Queens, New York, which is bound by the Cross Island Parkway on the West, Grand Central Parkway on the South, the New York City line on the East, and the Long Island Sound on the North. (B) To provide, at cost, first-aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) courses to the community when available.
resources.social: Facebook: @LNDCACEMS; Instagram: @lndcac; Linkedin: @Little Neck Douglaston Community Ambulance; Corps; Twitter: @lndcac
resources.fees: LNDCAC will never charge patients directly. CPR certifications courses are at cost.

resources.name: Living Faith Community Development Corporation
resources.address: 223-01 Union Turnpike, Lower Level Oakland Gardens, NY 11364
resources.mission: We are a nonprofit organization committed to the support, upliftment and growth of our neighbors in Flushing, New York. We seek to accomplish neighborhood revitalization in Flushing and beyond by mobilizing our community towards service and giving as an expression of God's love and generosity towards us. We aim to build a faithful presence in our community through development work rooted in advocacy and compassion. We desire to effect lasting impact by providing individuals and families with the service, skills and security that are needed to flourish. The Girls Outdoor Adventure Team (GOAT) is a youth program engaging high school girls in the Flushing community through outdoor exploration. GOAT offers these young women the chance to experience New York City's parks and natural spaces, participate in activities like hiking, biking, and kayaking, and build confidence, friendships, and leadership skills along the way. We meet once a week on Saturday mornings.
